candidates.abstract: RNA-derived 2′,3′-cyclophosphate-terminated nucleotides act as immune signalling molecules in prokaryotes and eukaryotes1–3, but how plants perceive them remains unknown. Sucking insects inject digestive enzymes including RNases into the host plant to acquire nutrients. Here we demonstrate that NIB1, a glycine-rich RNA-binding protein in rice, senses 2′,3′-cyclic nucleotide monophosphates (2′,3′-cNMPs; 2′,3′-cAMP and 2′,3′-cGMP) and adenylyl-(3′→5′)-guanosine 2′,3′-cyclic phosphate (ApG>p) produced by a salivary T2 ribonuclease of green stink bug during feeding. Binding of the RNase products promotes formation of nuclear condensates containing NIB1, which recruit the core immune regulator Enhanced Disease Susceptibility 1 (EDS1) and activate defence, potentially contributing to the immune signalling of Toll/interleukin-1 receptor (TIR) proteins that also produce the nuclease products. Exogenous application of 2′,3′-cAMP, 2′,3′-cGMP or ApG>p elicits NIB1 and EDS1-mediated immune responses. Our findings unveil a conserved pathway in plants, in which glycine-rich RNA-binding proteins perceive the nuclease-generated second messengers to launch defence and point to a potential link between plant TIR nuclease activity and EDS1 signalling. candidates.title: Domain-alteration chimeras rewire oncogenic complexes in prostate cancer
candidates.authors: Jie Luo, Jianzhang Yang, Jean Ching-Yi Tien, Mi Wang, Sumit Das, Xiaoju Wang, Eleanor Young, Jelena Tošović, Rahul Mannan, Weiguo Xiang, Xia Jiang, Jocelyn Cai, Yihan Liu, Kenneth Gu, Somnath Mahapatra, Shiting Li, Yitong Yin, Sanjana Eyunni, Abigail J. Todd, Shicheng Jin, Xuhong Cao, Fengyun Su, Stephanie J. Miner, Ranga Sudharshan, Arvind Rao, Abhijit Parolia, Yuanyuan Qiao, Shaomeng Wang, Arul M. Chinnaiyan
candidates.abstract: Abstract Transcriptional addiction to the androgen receptor (AR) underlies metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer 1 , in which AR maintains oncogenic programs through domain-specific interactions with the acetyltransferases p300 and CBP (collectively p300/CBP) 2 . Here we describe a novel therapeutic modality, domain-alteration chimeras (DALTACs), that rewire endogenous protein complexes by enforcing non-native domain–domain interactions. Our first-in-class AR–p300/CBP DALTAC-1 induces synthetic proximity between the ligand-binding domain of AR and the bromodomain of p300/CBP, misconfiguring their native interface and locking the complex in a non-productive state. DALTAC-1 triggers a ‘super-inhibitory’ effect, suppressing AR-driven transcription and proliferation more potently than combined AR and p300/CBP inhibition. Mechanistically, DALTAC-1 reprograms p300/CBP substrate engagement, abolishing the histone mark H2B N-terminal acetylation and inducing neomorphic acetylation of AR and coactivators, ultimately collapsing the AR neo-enhanceosome. Chromatin profiling revealed redistribution of AR and p300/CBP towards palindromic androgen response elements, accompanied by disruption of cofactor and transcriptional machinery recruitment at oncogenic AR and ERG neo-enhancers. DALTAC-1 exhibits exquisite lineage selectivity, displaying potent activity in AR–p300/CBP dual-dependent cells and sparing AR-negative cells. In multiple in vivo models, DALTAC-1 induces deep and durable tumour regressions. Together, these findings establish DALTACs as a broadly applicable strategy to rewire disease-defining complexes through domain-topology alteration, expanding induced-proximity therapies, and the precise lineage selectivity of DALTAC-1 supports its translational potential in AR-driven prostate cancer.

candidates.title: Independent interferometric observable confirms black hole shadow in M87*
candidates.authors: Samuel Lai, Nithyanandan Thyagarajan, O. Ivy Wong, Foivos Diakogiannis
candidates.abstract: Abstract A new epoch for direct visualization of accretion dynamics near the event horizon of a black hole began when the Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration synthesized an Earth-sized aperture with millimetre radio interferometry and published the first reconstructed image 1–4 of a black hole shadow at the core of radio galaxy Messier 87 (M87). The image appeared as a ring-like structure, representing the gravitationally lensed and redshifted emission around the central supermassive black hole, M87*, located at the galactic nucleus. However, application of various data analysis and imaging heuristics resulted in divergent representations of M87* fine-scale features 3,5–7 , with some external analyses even challenging the fundamental ring-like morphology of the source 8,9 . Such difficulties arise as a consequence of the inherent sparsity of the very long baseline interferometry measurements, making interferometric image reconstruction an inadequately constrained problem. Moreover, the solution is sensitive to instrument calibration, post-processing algorithms and imaging hyperparameters. Here we apply an independent imaging algorithm that we have developed to the M87* dataset that is free from prescriptive morphological priors and founded on observables immune to instrument calibration errors. We reconstruct the black hole shadow image and unequivocally reproduce a ring-like morphology, with an angular diameter of 42.2 ± 1.5 μas corresponding to a black hole mass of 6.5 ± 0.5 billion solar masses assuming nominal scaling parameters, observed at an inclination angle of approximately 20° from the approaching jet.

candidates.authors: Gregory P. Donaldson, Gabriella Lima dos Reis, Marwa Saad, Christopher Wichmann, Izabela Mamede, Guo Chen, Caroline E. Harrer, Nicole L. DelGaudio, Dayu Zhang, Begüm Aydin, Tiago B. R. Castro, Sergei I. Grivennikov, Bernardo S. Reis, Elise G. Liu, Stephanie C. Eisenbarth, Kivanç Birsoy, Sohail F. Tavazoie, Beth M. Stadtmueller, Gabriel D. Victora, Daniel Mucida
candidates.abstract: Immunoglobulin A (IgA) is the most abundant antibody isotype produced by mammals, and has a specialized role in mucosal homeostasis1. IgA is constantly secreted into the intestinal lumen and binds to commensal microorganisms to regulate their colonization and function2,3, with unclear implications for health. IgA deficiency is common in humans, but difficult to study, because of its complex aetiology and comorbidities4–8. Here we use genetically and environmentally controlled mice to show that various models of IgA deficiency result in increased susceptibility to several models of endogenous colorectal cancer. Cellular and molecular analyses revealed that, in the absence of IgA, colonic epithelial cells induce antibacterial factors and accelerate cell cycling in response to the microbiota. Oral treatment with IgA was sufficient to reduce steady-state proliferation and protect mice from tumours; however, this function was due to the structure of the antibody rather than to binding specificity. In a reductionist culture system, IgA directly suppressed epithelial growth. Co-immunoprecipitation mass spectrometry and targeted CRISPR screening identified DMBT1 as an IgA-binding epithelial surface protein that is required for IgA-mediated suppression of proliferation. Together, IgA and DMBT1 tune the normal cycling of absorptive colonocyte progenitors. In IgA-knockout mice, deleting the transmembrane and cytoplasmic signalling portions of DMBT1 was sufficient to reverse both the increased epithelial cell proliferation and the increased tumour susceptibility seen in these mice. These experiments establish a homeostatic function for IgA in tempering physiological epithelial responses to the microbiota to maintain mucosal health. Experiments in mouse models show that immunoglobulin A in the gut lumen has a role in regulating the turnover of colon epithelial cells and reduces the susceptibility of mice to colorectal cancer.

candidates.title: Glycosylation and importins liquefy the FG barrier in live nuclear pores
candidates.authors: Miao Yu, Maziar Heidari, Karen Palacio-Rodriguez, Hao Ruan, Sara Mingu, Yu Chen, Xu-Zhuo Gou, Pingkai Shen, Songzi Liu, Si-Yu Chen, Alam Ahmad Hidayat, Mathis Bode, Mateusz Sikora, Ai-Hui Tang, Gerhard Hummer, Edward A. Lemke
candidates.abstract: Abstract The nuclear pore complex (NPC) regulates molecular traffic between nucleus and cytoplasm 1,2 . Its permeability barrier is formed by intrinsically disordered phenylalanine-glycine-rich nucleoporins (FG-NUPs), whose physical state has long been debated 3–13 . Deciphering how FG-NUPs behave inside living cells is crucial for understanding how NPCs achieve both selective and rapid transport. By combining site-specific labelling with time-resolved fluorescence anisotropy, here we show that FG domains exhibit nanosecond-scale, liquid-like segmental motion in live cells, whereas reconstituted FG condensates undergo a liquid-to-solid transition in vitro. Experiments and molecular-dynamics simulations further show that importin-β, a principal nuclear transport receptor, and O-linked β- N -acetylglucosamine, a key post-translational modification of FG-NUPs, together stabilize the dynamic FG network. Finely balanced FG–FG and FG–importin-β interactions maintain FG-NUP liquidity and generate a radial organization in which importin-β is enriched near the NPC periphery and extended FG domains remain in the central channel, forming the transport barrier. This organization explains recent MINFLUX observations 14 of rim-biased transport trajectories and is supported here by direct MINFLUX imaging of importin-β in mammalian cells. Together, our results reconcile conflicting models of FG-NUP organization 4,5,7,9,15 and establish a framework for understanding how cellular context tunes intrinsically disordered proteins in health and disease.

candidates.title: Bureaucratic incentives shaped effectiveness of the one-child policy in China
candidates.authors: Lingsheng Meng, Hanmo Yang, Grant Miller, Hongbin Li
candidates.abstract: Empirical research so far largely suggests that population policies around the world do not explain a majority of the global fertility decline1–10. Notably, even China’s total fertility rate declined little after implementation of the one-child policy in 1979 and 1980, but fertility then fell sharply by more than one-third during the early 1990s. Here we show that strengthening bureaucratic incentives under China’s one vote veto policy, which strictly prohibited career advancement for adherence failure, was instrumental in more effective implementation of the one-child policy, and in its delayed impact on fertility. Using provincial variation in implementation timing, we find that the one vote veto explains nearly half of China’s total fertility rate decline during the 1990s, driving fertility below the replacement rate. Increases in use of intrauterine devices (the most prevalent form of modern contraception in China) that were recommended by local officials were particularly salient. Overall, our findings suggest that population policy, when more strictly enforced due to stronger bureaucratic incentives, made a greater contribution to low fertility in China than suggested by past research. Here we pair in vivo microplastic measurements with high-resolution tracking data from lowland tapirs and giant anteaters across Brazil and show that the microplastic burdens carried by free-ranging mammals increase with both the magnitude of their human footprint exposure and their proximity to development and waste management infrastructure. candidates.abstract: Abstract The global transition towards sustainable energy systems has identified tidal power as a uniquely predictable and substantial renewable energy resource 1 . However, the highly unsteady sea environment subjects turbines to severe hydrodynamic loads, greatly increasing capital and maintenance costs 2,3 . Large-scale state-of-the-art turbines at present rely on complex, expensive active pitch systems to mitigate these fluctuations. Here we present a reliable, passive alternative: flexible rubber blades featuring chordwise trailing-edge deformation. We experimentally demonstrate that these flexible blades achieve an equivalent total energy yield over simulated tidal cycles compared with rigid blades with active pitch control, while mitigating high-frequency fatigue-inducing load fluctuations by up to one-third. This passive load regulation arises from aeroelastic deformation that flattens blade camber under load, enabling structural robustness without added mechanical complexity. These findings suggest that chordwise-flexible blades can enhance the durability and performance of tidal turbines, offering a promising pathway towards more reliable and cost-effective tidal energy generation.

candidates.abstract: Abstract Unique molecular identifiers (UMIs) are widely utilised in RNA-sequencing (RNA-seq) technologies to eliminate polymerase chain reaction (PCR) duplicates, thereby improving the accuracy of molecular quantification. However, synthesis errors in UMIs during sequencing often compromise the reliability of UMI counting. While various computational methods have been developed for error correction, the lack of a unified benchmarking and validation framework impedes systematic evaluation and optimisation. Here, we present UMIche, an open-source, UMI-centric computational platform designed to enhance UMI-assisted molecular quantification. Its application to collapsing monomer and homotrimer UMIs across multiple bulk and single-cell sequencing protocols demonstrates effective PCR-duplicate removal. Across a broad spectrum of simulated and experimental datasets with ground truth, most UMI collapsing methods integrated into UMIche perform similarly under low-error conditions, whereas set-cover optimisation and majority voting show greater robustness as the UMI error profile becomes more pronounced. Together, these capabilities enable scalable UMI collapsing, systematic benchmarking, and method development to improve molecular quantification.

candidates.authors: Phuong Thao Le, Gaeun Yun, Tae Sik Hwang, Hyoun Wook Lee, Hyeokjin Cho, Jungho Lee, Geunbae Lim

candidates.title: Experience modifies the synaptome architecture in the developing and adult mouse brain
candidates.authors: Hanan Woods, Ülkü Günar, Sarah Catherine Gillard, Beverley Notman, Kunhao Yuan, Digin Dominic, Emily Robson, Gabor Varga, Noboru H. Komiyama, Zhen Qiu, Frank Sengpiel, Seth G. N. Grant
candidates.abstract: Abstract Synaptome architecture describes the spatiotemporal distribution of highly diverse excitatory synapses throughout the brain. Whether and how this architecture is impacted by experience and sensory input is unknown. We found that environmental enrichment and monocular visual deprivation drive large-scale reconfiguration of excitatory synapse populations in more than one hundred regions of the mouse brain. Different experiences modify distinct subsets of synapse types and subtypes, with patterns aligned with protein turnover rates and connectome architecture. Similarity in experience-dependent reconfiguration during development and adulthood indicates shared mechanisms of synaptome adaptation across the lifespan. Our findings support a population-selection model in which experiences drive adaptation by selectively modifying synapse types and subtypes distributed across the brain. Experience-driven reconfiguration of synaptome architecture shares features with the response to aging, sleep deprivation, brain injury and genetic mutations, supporting a unifying principle of brain adaptation.

candidates.abstract: RHOA, a RAS superfamily member, is frequently mutated in peripheral T-cell lymphoma (PTCL). These mutations are puzzling because variants have opposite effects on conventional RHOA signaling: some (e.g., RHOAG17V) inhibit normal RHOA function, whereas others (e.g., RHOAC16R) are constitutively active. Here we show that all PTCL-associated RHOA mutants acquire a non-canonical VAV1-like activity that activates the transcription factor NFAT. This activity is mediated by complexes between mutant RHOA and the RAP1GDS1607 isoform, is enhanced by T-cell receptor stimulation, and requires components of the T-cell receptor–VAV1 pathway, including PLCγ1 and calcineurin. Unlike canonical RAS superfamily signaling, this neomorphic activity does not require prenylation, the lipid modification anchoring RHOA to membranes. Genetic or pharmacological disruption of this pathway impairs RHOA-mutant PTCL in mouse models and patient-derived cells. These findings explain how mutations with opposing canonical effects converge on a shared oncogenic mechanism and reveal a potential therapeutic vulnerability in RHOA-mutant PTCL. candidates.title: Frequency-tagged fMRI reveals dual mechanisms of attentional enhancement and suppression
candidates.authors: Reebal W. Rafeh, Geoffrey N. Ngo, Lyle E. Muller, Ali R. Khan, Ravi S. Menon, Marieke Mur, Taylor W. Schmitz
candidates.abstract: Selective attention biases competition between concurrent visual inputs, yet its computational implementation in the human cortex remains unclear. Using frequency-tagged fMRI (ft-fMRI), we resolve how attention shapes the spatiotemporal dynamics of competing stimulus-driven responses at fine spatial scales. Distinct cortical populations exhibit either in-phase synchronization (target enhancement) or anti-phase synchronization (surround suppression) with attended stimuli. Population receptive field mapping reveals a target–surround organization, with in-phase populations biased toward the attended target and anti-phase populations biased toward the surrounding visual field. Directed attention uniformly amplifies surround suppression across the visual hierarchy, consistent with a distributed suppressive field, whereas modulation of target-related activity increases hierarchically from V1 to hV4. Critically, modulation of surround suppression, but not target enhancement, predicts behavioral performance. These findings dissociate the mechanisms of target enhancement and surround suppression and reveal the computational architecture underlying biased competition in the human cortex, converging with recent primate electrophysiology research. Rafeh et al. use frequency-tagged fMRI to demonstrate that selective attention relies on dual, independent neural mechanisms for target enhancement and surround suppression, elaborating on traditional unitary models of human visual attention.

candidates.title: Ferrocene heteroconjugation enables charge transport in DNA monolayers
candidates.authors: Koji Nakano, Tomiyuki Tsuruta
candidates.abstract: DNA has emerged as a promising self-assembling material for molecular electronics. Here, we investigate the electrical response of double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) modified with a ferrocene-functionalised psoralen that forms a covalent cross-link at TA–AT sites. A thiol-modified 10-mer DNA conjugate self-assembles on Au substrates, enabling simultaneous mapping of surface topography and current distribution by conductive atomic force microscopy. Under the present experimental conditions, native dsDNA remained close to the current detection limit, whereas incorporation of ferrocene resulted in a measurable increase. Analysis of the current–voltage characteristics did not reveal a clear signature of a single dominant transport mechanism. At higher fields, the response was consistent with field-assisted charge injection across the molecular junction. These results indicate that ferrocene incorporation modifies the electronic response of the DNA assembly and influences charge transport across the molecular layer. This approach requires no pre-derivatisation of the DNA backbone and provides a versatile strategy for post-synthetic functionalisation. DNA is a promising self-assembling material for molecular electronics, but efficient charge injection remains challenging because of its deep HOMO energy level. Here, the authors develop a chemically defined DNA–ferrocene conjugate through covalent modification of a DNA duplex and demonstrate an enhanced electrical response. The resulting metal–DNA molecular junctions show how electronic functionality can be programmed by molecular design, providing a platform for quantitative comparison with theoretical models.

candidates.authors: Wenjie Li, Junying Xue, Peng Chen, Yongping Dai, Jing He, Ruihao Tan, Jifeng Ge, Tingyi Xia, Shengqi Wang, Zhaoyang Lin
candidates.abstract: Abstract Low-voltage and high-performance electronic devices based on two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors demand high-quality dielectrics with efficient capacitive gating. However, it currently relies on specially engineered atomic layer deposition (ALD) of ultrathin high- k HfO 2 and ZrO 2 , or high-temperature vapor-phase growth of 2D dielectrics with post-growth transfer process. Here, we report a facile solution-processed 2D dielectric with an ultra-low thermal budget (i.e., at room temperature), while delivering competitive device metrics (e.g., low operating voltage and small hysteresis). This is enabled by an organic-free colloidal ink of montmorillonite (MTM) in environmentally friendly water solvent, eliminating the need for organic ligands or surfactants and thus the post-deposition high-temperature thermal annealing. Specifically, all-solution-processed MoS 2 field-effect transistors with MTM dielectric exhibit a low operating voltage of 1 V and small hysteresis (down to 1 mV). The solution process is generally compatible with diverse n-type and p-type 2D semiconductors such as MoS 2 , MoSe 2 and WSe 2 . Moreover, the robust and reproducible MTM dielectric enables scalable device integration into logic circuits, including inverters, AND, NOR, and NAND gates, as well as static random-access memory (SRAM). The scalable room-temperature solution-processed 2D dielectric offers a route to all-solution-processed and low-voltage 2D electronics.

candidates.title: Near-infrared plasmonic response in hyperdoped silicon nanoantennas for all-silicon photodetection
candidates.authors: Rang Li, Yi Liu, Mohd Saif Shaikh, Xia Wang, Yordan Georgiev, Xiaoli Sun, Chi Pang, Kambiz Jamshidi, Manfred Helm, Yonder Berencén, Shengqiang Zhou, Feng Chen
candidates.abstract: Abstract Plasmonic materials enable subwavelength confinement of light through the collective response of free carriers, but their operational spectral range is typically constrained by intrinsic carrier densities. Hyperdoped semiconductors offer a route to engineer plasmonic properties within a CMOS-compatible platform, yet their plasmonic response in silicon remains largely limited to the mid-infrared. Here we show that nanoantenna engineering extends the plasmonic response of phosphorus-hyperdoped silicon toward the near-infrared. The nanoantenna arrays exhibit tunable, polarization-dependent resonances in the 1–2 μm range, arising from geometry-driven localized modes on a Drude-like electronic background. Leveraging these effects, we realize all-silicon photoconductive detectors operating at 1.55 μm and room temperature, with a maximum bias-assisted responsivity of 0.58 A/W at 0.5 V. This response arises from plasmon-enhanced sub-bandgap absorption combined with trap-assisted photoconductive gain and therefore does not represent the intrinsic quantum efficiency. These results extend the spectral functionality of silicon photonics beyond its intrinsic absorption limits for integrated sensing, imaging, and optical communication.

candidates.title: Processing-induced self-organised triboelectric interfaces enable event-responsive cementitious composites
candidates.authors: Jingming Cai, Haolang Sun, Daiqi Li, Jiaqi Huang, Guangming Cai, Jing Wu, Hailiang Fei, Chang Wu, Liyun Ma, Liangzhu Leon Wang, Y. X. Zhang, Ruijun Zhang, Tong Guo
candidates.abstract: Structural materials are commonly designed to bear loads passively, whereas sensing and energy-harvesting functions are typically implemented using externally attached devices that are vulnerable to damage and interfacial failure. Here we report a processing-induced strategy for forming self-organised triboelectric interfaces directly within fibre-reinforced cementitious composites during vibration-assisted casting. Through fresh-state flow, fibre migration, and grid-assisted interception, conductive and dielectric constituents assemble into local fibre-enriched contact regions, enabling intrinsic electromechanical transduction without post-fabrication assembly. Microstructural characterisation reveals local fibre enrichment and fibre-grid interweaving around the embedded coated grid, while first-principles calculations support the interfacial charge redistribution between polyvinyl alcohol and polytetrafluoroethylene. The composites retain high mechanical toughness while exhibiting stable electrical responses under low-frequency mechanical excitation, with signal amplitude scaling with load and contact configuration. After cracking, newly created internal interfaces continue to provide functional output, demonstrating damage-tolerant electromechanical activity. We further demonstrate an event-triggered sensing system in which the embedded interfaces serve as self-powered signal sources for wake-up and alert operations. This work establishes a processing-driven route for programming functional interfaces within structural materials and provides a basis for intrinsically responsive infrastructure components. The study shows that vibration-assisted casting forms fibre-polymer contacts inside a cementitious composite, enabling electrical signals after damage and a laboratory demonstration of event-triggered alerts.

candidates.authors: Tarun Patel, Matteo Pennacchietti, Sayan Gangopadhyay, Dan Dalacu, Philip J. Poole, Stephen Hughes, Michael E. Reimer
candidates.abstract: Abstract Single-atom waveguide-QED systems have emerged as a leading platform for demonstrating non-linear optics in the few-photon regime. Devices with such non-linear behavior are necessary for developing deterministic gates for photonic quantum computing. Artificial atoms coupled to nanophotonic or superconducting waveguides can be used to engineer highly efficient light-matter interfaces for such non-linear interactions, where every photon in the system interacts with the quantum emitter. However, it has been a challenge to access the reflection port of the waveguide due to the inability of rejecting stray electromagnetic fields that do not interact with the artificial atom. Here, we show coherent reflection of single photons from a semiconductor quantum dot strongly coupled to the fundamental waveguide mode of a nanowire. We utilize the tapered end of the nanowire for ideal mode-matching in a vertical geometry, enabled by the extinction technique developed. This mode-matching allows for efficient transfer of photons from the input to the reflection port while having all interacted with the quantum dot. Such a high-efficiency scalable photonic platform opens up applications in few-photon quantum nonlinear optics and has been proposed for creating key resource states for universal photon-based quantum computing.

candidates.title: Probing topological edge states in a molecular synthetic dimension
candidates.authors: Adarsh P. Raghuram, Francesca M. Blondell, Jonathan M. Mortlock, Benjamin P. Maddox, Sohail Dasgupta, Holly A. J. Middleton-Spencer, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Hannah M. Price, Philip D. Gregory, Simon L. Cornish
candidates.abstract: Abstract Synthetic dimensions, where additional spatial dimensions are encoded within the internal states of a quantum system, allow the realisation of phenomena usually inaccessible in experiments. Ultracold polar molecules are an ideal platform for synthetic dimensions, providing large Hilbert spaces of long-lived rotational and hyperfine states that can be linked with microwave fields to simulate tunnelling. Here, we realise a one-dimensional synthetic lattice using the rotational states of ultracold RbCs molecules and investigate the topological properties of the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model. We spectroscopically probe the system using an auxiliary rotational state and study the time dynamics after deterministic state preparation. We demonstrate long coherence times, reaching ~ 500 tunnelling periods even for lattices spanning eight rotational states. Using full site-resolved readout over long evolution times, we study the robustness of topologically protected edge states against perturbations that preserve or break chiral symmetry. These results establish ultracold molecules as a powerful platform for quantum simulation using synthetic dimensions.

candidates.authors: Yu Guo, Yue Ma, Qichang Jin, Chuan Gan, Jun Zhang, Huazhen Rong, Tao Liu, Ning Wang, Yihui Yuan
candidates.abstract: Sustainable uranium supply is critical for nuclear energy, yet its practical recovery is severely hindered by the chemical complexity of uranium in natural waters. This dual-adaptive mechanism enables rapid, selective, and high-capacity uranium extraction across diverse aqueous chemistries and offers a general strategy for recognizing multiple metal species in complex environments. Uranium recovery is hindered by the chemical complexity of uranium ions in natural waters. Here the authors report a geometrically and chemically dual-adaptive three-dimensional covalent organic framework which enables rapid and selective uranium-extraction across diverse aqueous chemistries.

candidates.title: Nudix protein D250R promotes African swine fever virus infection by disrupting host ubiquitination machinery
candidates.authors: Jiwen Zhang, Menglong Cao, Renqiang Liu, Linfei Song, Zhenjiang Zhang, Fangyuan Zhang, Runyi Yao, Liqin Yang, Dongdong Shen, Yuanmao Zhu, Encheng Sun, Xijun He, Fang Li, Zhigao Bu, Xiangpeng Sheng, Dongming Zhao
candidates.abstract: Numerous viruses have evolved diverse strategies to counteract host antiviral responses. African swine fever virus (ASFV), a large double-stranded DNA virus that threatens the global swine industry and food security, is thought to employ highly complex yet poorly understood mechanisms to facilitate infection. Here, we identify a previously uncharacterized strategy by which ASFV evades host antiviral defenses and maintains virulence. We show that ASFV infection progressively impairs the assembly of ubiquitin conjugates in host cells and that the ASFV-encoded Nudix protein D250R acts as a potent suppressor of cellular ubiquitination. Expression of D250R disrupts the host ubiquitination machinery in a manner dependent on its intact structure. Mechanistically, D250R directly binds ATP via its Nudix domain and inhibits ATP-dependent, E1-mediated ubiquitin activation, thereby suppressing ubiquitination-driven antiviral immune responses and promoting viral replication. Genetic deletion of the D250R gene markedly attenuates ASFV virulence while eliciting robust immune responses in pigs. Notably, immunization with the D250R-deficient virus confers complete protection against lethal challenge with a virulent ASFV strain. Collectively, these findings reveal a previously unrecognized viral strategy to subvert host immunity and establish the D250R-deleted ASFV as a promising live-attenuated vaccine candidate for African swine fever control. This study uncovers a novel African swine fever virus (ASFV) immune-evasion mechanism targeting ubiquitin activation and identifies D250R as a key virulence factor. Loss of D250R attenuates the virus and supports its potential as a live attenuated vaccine candidate against ASF.

candidates.authors: Lei Huang, Zhehan Yi, Tao Xiao, Jin-Lin Yang, Zefang Yang, Yiren Cheng, Shixing Yuan, Wulong Li, Long Chen, Xuhui Zhou, Hong Jin Fan, Lei Wei
candidates.abstract: Abstract Four-electron iodine redox chemistry offers a high theoretical specific energy of ~1324 Wh kgI −1 , yet its practical realization is fundamentally limited by the conflicting demands of rapid I 0 /I + oxidation, effective suppression of iodine shuttling, and stabilization of highly reactive I + species. Here we report a redox-active, Lewis acid/base-tunable phthalimide that resolves these constraints through a single-molecule polarity-switching mechanism. Upon electrochemical oxidation, electrophilic phthalimide δ+ strongly interacts with nucleophilic iodine and polyiodide species, concurrently suppressing polyiodide shuttling and promoting their conversion to I + . The consecutively generated phthalimide δ− acts as a nucleophilic stabilizer for the resulting I + species. This electrochemically driven polarity switching of phthalimide enables flexible four-electron Li-I 2 pouch cells that deliver ~400 mAh gI −1 capacity, a specific energy exceeding 1200 Wh kgI −1 , a high cathode-level specific energy ( ~ 883.4 Wh kg(cathode) −1 ), and stable cycling over 1000 cycles. The successful integration of these cells into wearable wireless charging and motion-sensing systems demonstrates the potential of polarity-switchable iodine chemistry for next-generation flexible energy-storage devices.

candidates.title: Robust optical skyrmion arising from randomness
candidates.authors: Zhuoyi Wang, Xingyuan Lu, Peng Shi, Xiaotan Lu, Zhenyang Xia, Qiwen Zhan, Yangjian Cai, Xiaocong Yuan, Chengliang Zhao
candidates.abstract: Optical skyrmions, known as topological quasiparticles, have emerged as a distinct photonic degree of freedom with great potential and promising prospects for broad applications. Prior studies have predominantly focused on skyrmions in fully coherent light fields. In this paper, we show that incoherent optical skyrmions can arise from an ensemble of random modes whose statistical correlations are deliberately engineered. Under external obstacles, the engineered statistical correlations enable reconstruction of the focal field, while the skyrmion topology provides a quantized global measure of the structural robustness. Beyond enabling programmable control over skyrmion topology by tailoring these correlations, the statistical construction suppresses the fixed-phase interference between neighboring skyrmion units inherent in coherent superpositions. The demonstrated robustness under obstacles, enhanced skyrmion density resolution, and flexible generation of programmable arrays extensively expand the skyrmion family and offer insights into optical quasiparticles, with potential applications in photonics. This study shows that optical skyrmions can emerge from engineered correlations among random light modes, retain their topology under strong obstruction, and form densely packed programmable arrays.

candidates.title: Activation of high-lying dormant states by cascaded transition control in core@shell upconversion nanoparticles
candidates.authors: Jun Zeng, Tong Chen, Huilin Liu, Yunfei Shang, Fenglin Wang, Xiaoyong Huang, Shuwei Hao, Jiajia Zhou, Chunhui Yang
candidates.abstract: Lanthanide-doped upconversion nanoparticles exhibit multicolor emission through discrete, narrowband transitions, enabling applications in bioimaging, lasers, and displays. However, the trade-off between leveraging abundant energy levels for multicolor output and mitigating rapid deactivation of high-lying states remains a fundamental challenge for achieving balanced white-light emission under moderate excitation power. This is particularly true for emitters such as Ho3+, which are highly susceptible to severe multiphonon relaxation and back energy transfer. Here, we address this by introducing a core@shell cascaded transition strategy that selectively populates Ho3+ high-lying states via engineered energy relays at a key intermediate level, Ce3+-mediated cross-relaxation control, and precise spatial ion arrangement. Our design achieves a ∼1500-fold boost in blue emission versus conventional architectures, enabling balanced red, green and blue output at 10 W/cm2 (10 mg/mL suspension). This white-light system surpasses mixed-nanoparticle media in stability, producing white lasers for photonics. Our approach provides a versatile route to high-lying states activation in lanthanide systems, with potential implications for multicolor imaging, displays, and anti-counterfeiting. The authors develop triply doped upconversion nanoparticles with cascaded energy transition pathways via precise spatial ion arrangement, which enables balanced RGB multicolor output and white lasing.

candidates.title: Pigment repression protects fungus from ferroptosis to maintain virulence
candidates.authors: Yaping Zhu, Tianling Ma, Jiayi Zhou, Kewei Sun, Zhiheng Zhou, Yiqing Li, Xia Chen, Xinyu Huang-Fu, Hubertus Haas, Zhonghua Ma, Yanni Yin
candidates.abstract: Fungal pathogens must adapt to host-derived stresses to establish infection, yet how secondary metabolite regulation contributes to this process remains poorly understood. Here, we show that Fusarium graminearum, a major cereal pathogen, suppresses the pigment aurofusarin biosynthetic gene cluster in response to host-derived iron excess, thereby preventing rubrofusarin-mediated ferroptosis and promoting invasive growth within wheat tissues. Rubrofusarin directly reacts with Fe²⁺ to form iron oxide complexes, resulting in intracellular iron accumulation, lipid peroxidation, and ferroptosis. Mechanistically, host-derived iron stress activates the HOG-MAPK pathway, leading to Hog1-dependent phosphorylation of the transcription factor FgSR. Phosphorylated FgSR recruits the histone deacetylase FgRpd3 to the aurofusarin biosynthetic gene cluster, establishing a repressive chromatin state that limits rubrofusarin production. Our findings reveal epigenetic repression of secondary metabolism as an adaptive strategy that enables fungal pathogens to withstand host-imposed iron stress, evade ferroptosis, and maintain virulence. The phytopathogenic fungus Fusarium graminearum produces a secondary metabolite, aurofusarin, at late stages during wheat infection. Here, the authors show how the biosynthesis of aurofusarin is regulated to avoid host-induced iron stress that results from the formation of iron complexes by an aurofusarin intermediate.

candidates.title: ATR promotes genome instability via CENP-A eviction from centromeres after prolonged exposure to genotoxic stress
candidates.authors: Denis Ostapenko, Hang Li, Isabelle Trier, Ross Shamby, Yanhua Wang, Eleanor Zagoren, Carla Becerra Sabrera, Kaelyn Sumigray, Claudio R. Alarcón, Lilian Kabeche
candidates.abstract: DNA damage in interphase leads to genome instability in part by promoting missegregation of chromosomes lacking centromeres. Yet the complete molecular mechanisms linking DNA damage to centromere dysfunction remain incompletely understood. Here, we show that prolonged exposure to genotoxic stress induces eviction of the histone H3 variant CENP-A. Displaced CENP-A relocalizes to nucleoli. This process depends on the DNA damage response kinase ATR and occurs in both human and mouse cells. We show that ATR promotes CENP-A eviction by promoting the nuclear localization of the AAA+ ATPase VCP through phosphorylation of Ser784, thereby destabilizing CENP-A-containing nucleosomes. Moreover, CENP-A localization to nucleoli relies on the nucleolar protein NPM1 and the canonical CENP-A chaperone HJURP, but not the H3 histone chaperones DAXX or ATRX. Importantly, ATR-dependent CENP-A eviction persists after cell-cycle re-entry and correlates with the emergence of CENP-A-deficient chromosomes, thereby linking DNA damage directly to segregation defects. Our findings identify a role for ATR in regulating centromere identity under stress and describe a mechanistic pathway that contributes to genome instability. Interphase DNA damage can lead to genome instability by promoting missegregation of chromosomes lacking centromeres. Here the authors show that DNA damage activates ATR and driving VCP-dependent eviction of CENP-A from centromeres to nucleoli. CENP-A loss causes increased chromosomes missegregation, linking DNA damage to centromere dysfunction.
